#!/usr/bin/env bash
# find_hosts.sh - simple ping sweep to list active IPs in a subnet
#
# Usage:
#   ./find_hosts.sh 192.168.1.0/24
#   ./find_hosts.sh 192.168.1    # treated as 192.168.1.0/24
#   ./find_hosts.sh              # defaults to first /24 from routing table
#
# Output:
#   Prints responsive IPs, one per line.

set -euo pipefail

is_cmd() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

usage() {
  sed -n '1,35p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
  exit 2
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  usage
fi

input="${1:-}"

# Determine subnet
subnet=""

if [[ -n "$input" ]]; then
  if [[ "$input" =~ ^([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}/[0-9]{1,2}$ ]]; then
    subnet="$input"
  elif [[ "$input" =~ ^([0-9]{1,3}\.){2}[0-9]{1,3}$ ]]; then
    subnet="$input.0/24"
  else
    die "Unsupported subnet format: '$input' (use a.b.c.d/nn or a.b.c)"
  fi
else
  # Pick a sane default: first non-loopback IPv4 route src, assume /24
  if is_cmd ip; then
    # Try to infer from default route first
    src=$(ip -4 route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="src") {print $(i+1); exit}}' || true)
    if [[ -z "${src:-}" ]]; then
      src=$(ip -4 addr show scope global 2>/dev/null | awk '/inet /{print $2}' | head -n1 | cut -d/ -f1 || true)
    fi
  else
    src=""
  fi
  [[ -n "${src:-}" ]] || die "Could not auto-detect local IPv4 address; pass a subnet like 192.168.1.0/24"
  subnet="${src%.*}.0/24"
fi

# We only support /24 in this lightweight script (common home/office).
if [[ ! "$subnet" =~ ^([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}/24$ ]]; then
  die "Only /24 subnets are supported right now (got '$subnet')"
fi

base="${subnet%/24}"
prefix="${base%.*}"

# Ping settings: keep it quick.
# - Linux iputils ping: -c 1 (one packet), -W 1 (1s timeout)
# - macOS/BSD ping: -c 1, -W is ms there; use -t 1 as TTL + rely on default timeout.

ping_one() {
  local ip="$1"
  if ping -c 1 -W 1 "$ip" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "$ip"
    return 0
  fi
  # fallback for macOS/BSD if -W unsupported
  if ping -c 1 "$ip" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "$ip"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

# Concurrency control
jobs=${JOBS:-64}

# Disable set -e around wait to avoid failing if some pings fail
set +e

pids=()

tmp=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

for i in $(seq 1 254); do
  ip="$prefix.$i"
  (
    ping_one "$ip"
  ) >>"$tmp" &
  pids+=("$!")

  # throttle
  if (( ${#pids[@]} >= jobs )); then
    wait "${pids[0]}" 2>/dev/null
    pids=("${pids[@]:1}")
  fi
done

# wait remaining
for pid in "${pids[@]}"; do
  wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
done

# Print unique sorted results
sort -Vu "$tmp"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Git hook: post-checkout
# Runs after `git checkout` changes HEAD or the working tree.
#
# WARNING: This will run a network ping sweep on every checkout.
# Disable by setting FIND_HOSTS_DISABLE=1

set -euo pipefail

if [[ "${FIND_HOSTS_DISABLE:-}" == "1" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)
if [[ -z "${repo_root:-}" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

script="$repo_root/find_hosts.sh"
if [[ ! -x "$script" ]]; then
  # script missing or not executable
  exit 0
fi

# Optional: pass a subnet via FIND_HOSTS_SUBNET
subnet="${FIND_HOSTS_SUBNET:-}"

# Run quietly; write results to a file so it doesn't spam every checkout.
outfile="$repo_root/active_hosts.txt"

if [[ -n "$subnet" ]]; then
  "$script" "$subnet" >"$outfile" || true
else
  "$script" >"$outfile" || true
fi
